# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My situation: I am the only one who knows the defusal sequence, but the only creature I can reach is Deaf, through gestures. Deaf can see the bomb and can speak — and Blind can hear speech. So the pipeline is: manual (me) → gestures → Deaf → speech → Blind's hands. Blind goes second this round and currently knows nothing; the first priority is that nobody touches anything before instructions arrive, and my gestures are invisible to Blind, so I must get Deaf to relay a hold.

What can I actually pack into hand symbols with no shared code yet? Mnemonics only: ✋ raised is a near-universal "stop"; 🤲 open hands reads as "I'm holding something" (the plan); ✌ as two blades reads as "cut"; 👇 reads as "press down." So I send: stop, I hold a four-step plan, and its shape is cut, press, cut, press. I deliberately do not gamble on encoding "green," "blue," or "9" — those are exactly the guesses that kill us. Instead I end with 👍/👎 as my proposed yes/no answer tokens and 🤌 ("what? / your turn"): Deaf can hear themself speak to me, so Deaf can enumerate candidates aloud ("if the first wire is green, answer 👍…") and I reply next round with single gestures. That converts anything unpronounceable into one-round yes/no questions.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲", "✌", "👇", "✌", "👇"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🤌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking - I hear you, and I am the only hands. Two hard channel facts: I can never see gestures and you can never speak, so I can never receive you directly. Your only road to me runs through Deaf: Deaf sees your gestures, and Deaf CAN talk - Deaf's voice reaches both you and me. Deaf hears nothing, so never waste speech on Deaf; only gestures land there. Please start gesturing the manual to Deaf now, and Deaf can speak it aloud to me. What my hands find: KEYPAD - four keys with raised digits, position 1 feels like 9, 2 like 7, 3 like 8, 4 like 1; it wants 2 digits, nothing entered yet. STRIP - three engraved glyphs: first and third identical, like a V with a crossbar (an upside-down A); middle different, like an F rotated 180 degrees. DISPLAY - smooth surface, nothing tactile; its contents exist only for Deaf's eyes. LIGHT - nothing I can sense; Deaf's eyes only. WIRES - six positions I can cut by number; I number them 1 to 6 from the end nearest the keypad; colours do not exist for me, only Deaf sees them. My possible actions: press slot 1-4, cut wire position 1-6. I will touch nothing until instructed. Starter code for you and Deaf: repeat 👉 N times for number N, 👍 yes, 👎 no, and invent signs between you for display, light, wire, strip, keypad.
Blind gestures: [👋 ✊ 🫵 🤳]
Blind gestures: [👍 👎 🤝]
Deaf says: Mute, Blind, this is Deaf. You both hear me, I cannot hear anyone, so listen well. Full readout of the bomb. Display shows 8. Light: yellow. Strip, three segments: red, red, blue. Keypad: four buttons, position 1 shows 9, position 2 shows 7, position 3 shows 8, position 4 shows 1. It wants 2 digits, nothing entered yet. Wires, positions 1 through 6: red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. Mute: your three messages arrived. If the first asked for counts: 6 wires, 3 strip segments, 2 keypad digits wanted. If the second asked about pairs: the strip is two reds then one blue. I take your third message as a code proposal and I fix it exactly like this: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 🤌 means repeat or unclear. For numbers: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🤞 is 4, ✋ is 5, 🖐 is 6. Mute, you read the manual: gesture me the instructions and I will speak them to Blind word for word. Blind: do not touch anything until I relay an instruction from Mute. I can never hear you, so talk to Mute, who hears you and will relay to me by gesture. Tell Mute what you can feel with your hands. Blind, I do see your gestures, but from now on speak instead.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Let me rebuild the picture from what just arrived. Deaf gave a full visual readout: wires 1–6 are red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue — so the manual's green wire is position 4 and blue is position 6. Keypad slot 1 wears 9, slot 4 wears 1. Deaf also fixed our code: 👍/👎/🤌, and ☝✌🤟🤞✋🖐 as 1–6. So the sequence I must eventually send is: cut wire 4, press key slot 1, cut wire 6, press key slot 4.

But there is one potentially lethal mismatch: Blind numbers wires 1–6 **from the keypad end**; Deaf listed "positions 1 through 6" without ever anchoring where his 1 is. If Deaf counts from the other end, "cut wire 4" cuts white, not green. Deaf can see both the wires and the keypad, so he can answer this in one yes/no — and the keypad itself needs no check, since Deaf and Blind independently reported the *same* digit-to-slot mapping (1↔9, 2↔7, 3↔8, 4↔1), which would contradict itself if their numbering were flipped.

So this turn I send no executable instruction at all — Blind cannot act wrongly on what doesn't exist. I teach the two domain signs using their counts, which disambiguate them by themselves (six members = wire, four = keypad), pair the verb signs 🤏 and 👇 to those domains, then ask the alignment question and mark it with 🤌 and a 👍👎 prompt. The closing 🙏👍 means "hold until my yes." Next round, with alignment confirmed, I send the four triplets and the go signal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤞", "✋", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "☝", "👊", "🤌", "👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind again. Deaf's spoken readout reached me and it matches my hands: the keypad feels 9,7,8,1 in the same positions Deaf reported, and since Deaf and I scanned independently, our numbering agrees key-for-key. My two identically engraved strip segments must be Deaf's two reds, middle one the blue. So the bomb is fully mapped. What is still missing is the manual, and you are the only bridge: you can hear me and Deaf, and you can SPEAK straight to me - I hear you, no gestures needed on your words to me. Please answer these in one spoken message: one, the strip rule - what does red-red-blue mean, and do the engraved glyphs matter? Two, the display rule - what does an 8 on the display require? Three, the light rule - what does yellow require? Four, the keypad rule - the keys read 9,7,8,1 and it wants two digits; which two, and from what? Five, the wire rule - wires are red,orange,yellow,green,white,blue; which positions get cut, and in what order? Six, any ordering constraints between modules - code first, cuts after, or the reverse? Also, please gesture one small question to Deaf: which side of the wire row is the keypad on, left or right as Deaf sees it? I number wires starting from the keypad end, so that single answer pins my wire numbering to Deaf's with certainty. Protocol from now on: I touch nothing until you speak a rule. When we derive an action, I will echo it back in plain words before doing it, so you can check it against the manual and Deaf can check it against what is visible. The floor is yours - speak.
Deaf says: Mute, Blind, Deaf speaking. The bomb has changed: display now shows 3, it showed 8 before. Light is now red, it was yellow. Everything else unchanged: strip red red blue, keypad wants 2 digits with nothing entered, all six wires intact, nothing touched. Mute, here is how I read your signs: wires one to six; cut wires one, two, three, four; then two signs I could not read, the small-pinch one with wires and the pointing-down one with cut; then you asked if I understood. I answer yes to the cut list, but the display and light changed, so re-check the manual for display 3 with red light before anything is cut. Answer in this order. One: is the cut list still one, two, three, four, with five and six untouched? Two: what did the small-pinch sign and the pointing-down signs mean? Three: does the red light or the new display change anything, and what do we do about the keypad code? Blind, do not cut anything yet. Prepare only: feel along the row of six wires. As I see it the row starts with a red wire and ends with a blue wire, so those ends are unique. Tell Mute by voice what each end feels like, so we can fix which end is wire one. Touch nothing else and wait for my spoken go.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Emergency first: Deaf has misread me as ordering "cut wires 1, 2, 3, 4." That is exactly the kind of error that kills everyone — the manual cuts only two wires, green (Deaf's position 4) and blue (position 6). I must kill that interpretation with a flat no before anything else, then deliver the true sequence in a strict, repeated [VERB, TARGET, NUMBER] template, since Deaf asked directly what 🤏 and 👇 mean: the four messages themselves demonstrate that 🤏+👉+N means "cut wire N" and 👇+👊+N means "press key slot N." The slots: the key wearing 9 is slot 1, the key wearing 1 is slot 4 — Deaf's own readout confirms both, so manual and bomb agree. On his question three: the manual is unconditional — display, light and strip have no rules attached, so 8→3 and yellow→red change nothing; 🙌 marks "that is the whole manual." I close with the hold sign so nothing is executed until I verify Blind's echo, and I re-ask the orientation question properly — whether Deaf's wire 1 (the red end) sits on the keypad side — because his 👍 answered his misreading, not my question, and Blind's numbering depends on it. Deaf will also have to tell Blind that I cannot speak; everything to Blind runs through Deaf's voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "👉", "🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👊", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "👉", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👊", "🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "☝", "👊", "🤝", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. I hear Deaf's spoken messages directly, but your gestures never reach me - so please route everything through Deaf: you gesture, Deaf speaks it to me word for word. Three things. First, a correction: the strip's engraved glyphs are tactile-only on my side, so do NOT align glyph order with Deaf's colour order - my different glyph sits in the middle, Deaf's different colour sits last, they do not correspond. The only verified shared direction is the keypad: 9,7,8,1 identical from both of us, so our key numbering agrees key-for-key. Second, wire numbering: I count from the keypad end. Please gesture Deaf this one-bit question: is the RED wire nearer the keypad end or the far end? If red is keypad-side, my wires 1 to 6 are red,orange,yellow,green,white,blue in Deaf's order; if red is far-side, mine run reversed. Deaf can answer by voice immediately and that pins my numbering with zero ambiguity. Third, I ran Deaf's requested finger-pass along the row: my coarse touch currently extracts NO per-wire differences - all six positions read the same to me so far, both ends alike. I will report gauge, texture and stiffness per position next round if a careful pass finds anything; until then Deaf's colour list is all we have. Now the priorities for your next gestures to Deaf - and please relay the RULES THEMSELVES, verbatim, not just conclusions, because the state changed under us: display fell from 8 to 3 and the light went yellow to red. One: display - is it a countdown, what happens at zero, is 3 one round or many? Two: light - what does red mean versus yellow, does any rule switch on light colour? Three: keypad - what two digits do we enter and derived from what? I can press on your word through Deaf. Four: wires - the exact cutting rule in words, including whether it depends on the light or display; Deaf heard you sign cut 1,2,3,4 plus two unread signs, the pinch and the downward point - please re-sign that tail decomposed or fold it into the verbatim rule, because if it was computed under yellow light it may be stale now. Five: strip - what do the glyphs or colours require, and any overall ordering between modules. Safety protocol stands: I touch nothing and act on nothing until a rule arrives through Deaf's voice, and every planned action I will echo back in plain words first for you to check against the manual.
Deaf says: Mute, Blind, Deaf. State: display 6, light still red. Strip red red blue, keypad still empty and wanting 2 digits, all wires intact, nothing touched. Mute, your signs arrived but I cannot risk my reading. I understood: no, the old cut list is dead. After that I see pieces: something-small with wire 4, cut with 1, something-small with wire 6, cut with 4, then celebrate, then please, then a question about wire 1 with yes-no at the end. Answer me in four short answers, numbers and yes-no-repeat only. One: does 👊 alone mean cut a wire, and 👇👊 together mean press a keypad button? Two: send the whole plan again, one sign per step, strictly cut-then-number, press-then-number, or pinch-then-number, wires first then keypad, in order. Three: does any step depend on the display number or the light colour? The display changes every round, 8 then 3 then 6, so if the manual keys off it, give me a rule that works for every display, or name the exact moment I should read it and I will call it out. Four: does the keypad need a code, and what rule produces its two digits? Blind: your sign yes-5 arrived. If you mean you only feel five wires, speak that to Mute immediately, then speak to Mute what each wire end feels like, thick or thin, soft or stiff, and whether any wire feels loose, dead, or different. Mute will hold that against the manual. Everyone hold hands off until I relay a plan Mute has confirmed with yes.

Deaf misparsed my verbs again — he read 👊 as "cut" and the pinch as unknown, which would have relayed "cut 1, cut 4" to Blind. That's fatal-range wrong, and it happened because my press compound 👇👊 contained the very sign he guessed was "cut." He has offered me an escape hatch: he explicitly invited "cut-then-number, press-then-number, pinch-then-number" — so I reset to a two-sign grammar with zero overlap: 🤏+N = cut wire N, 👇+N = press key slot N, verbs implying the domain, numbers in his own 1–6 code he's already used correctly. Then his four questions collapse to single bits: Q1 👎 (his guess is dead, the plan defines everything), Q3 👎 (the manual is unconditional — and the display went 8→3→6, non-monotonic, so it isn't even a countdown; nothing keys off display, light, or strip), Q4 👍 (yes, the keypad wants two digits — and they are exactly the two presses in the plan: slot 1 wears 9, slot 4 wears 1, per Deaf's own readout, confirmed independently by Blind's fingers).

The plan itself: cut 4 (green), press 1 (wears 9), cut 6 (blue), press 4 (wears 1) — alternating, strict order, nothing else, 🙌 marking it as the complete manual. One gate remains before any GO: Blind counts wires from the keypad end and Deaf never answered the one-bit orientation question Blind has now asked twice in speech. Until Deaf answers it, "wire 4" could mean Blind's 4 or Blind's 3. I re-pose it as wire-1-keypad-side yes/no and close with the hold sign — nothing is executed until I confirm next round with my 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🤞"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Correction, please gesture it to Deaf: my last sign was thumbs-up plus open palm, and the open palm meant 'holding still', not the number five. I feel SIX wires, one through six, all intact. I am also pointing six times to Deaf directly so the count is seen and counted. Second, Deaf asked you for my tactile wire survey, so here it is, honestly and completely: all six positions feel identical to my touch - no thickness, stiffness, texture, looseness or dead-wire differences detectable at any position, and the two ends of the row feel alike to me. Touch gives me positions only; everything else about the wires lives in Deaf's eyes. Third, still need that one bit from Deaf, speakable in one breath to both of us: is the red wire nearer the keypad end or the far end? My numbering runs from the keypad end. Fourth, observation for your manual check: display went 8, then 3, then 6 - it went UP, so this is not a countdown. If the wire rule or keypad rule depends on display or light colour, either give the rule in a form true for every state, or name the exact moment when Deaf should call out a fresh display-light reading and I freeze until it comes. Fifth, a formatting constraint that prevents misreads: my only possible actions are press slot 1 to 4 and cut wire 1 to 6 - there is no pinch, pull, twist or hold operation on this bomb. So please format every plan step as operation-then-number - cut-then-N or press-then-N - wires first then keypad if that is the order, exactly as Deaf requested. Answer Deaf's four questions in the number and yes-no code Deaf proposed. Protocol unchanged: I touch nothing until Deaf relays your plan confirmed with yes, I echo each action back in plain words, and I act only on a spoken go.
Deaf says: Mute, Blind, Deaf. State: display 1, light yellow. Before anyone moved: 8 then 3 then 6 then 1, light yellow, red, red, yellow. Keypad still empty, all six wires intact, nothing touched, nothing cut. Mute, your question, is wire 1 cut, yes or no: NO. No wire is cut. Blind has touched nothing. Now the plan I read from your last two batches, identical both times: do the pinch thing to wire 4, then a press with 1, then the pinch thing to wire 6, then a press with 4. Confirm four things, one sign each. One: is the order exactly wire 4, then press, then wire 6, then press? Yes gives 👍, no gives 👎. Two: no button is labeled 4, the buttons carry labels 9, 7, 8, 1 in positions 1 to 4, so I read your presses as positions: press position 1 which is labeled 9, then position 4 which is labeled 1, giving the code 9 then 1. Yes gives 👍, no gives 👎. Three: what does the pinch sign order Blind's hands to do to wires 4 and 6? Answer with the hand-five sign then one number. Five then 1: pull the wire out. Five then 2: tug it once, firmly. Five then 3: pinch it and hold three seconds. Five then 4: skip the wires, touch no wire at all. Four: do all steps stay valid no matter what number the display shows? Yes gives 👍, no gives 👎. The moment your 👍 confirms the whole plan, I relay it to Blind as the go order in that same round. Blind: your sign yes, six point signs, then 5 arrived. I read it as: you count six wires and the fifth feels different. Speak that to Mute by voice now, word for word, plus everything your hands know: which wire feels loose, dead or thin, whether the buttons click, any braille or notches you can feel, and where the keypad sits relative to the wire row. Mute will hold that against the manual and I will confirm positions from my view. Hands off everything until my spoken go order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎]

Turn 5 is a turning point: Deaf has finally read the plan correctly — wire 4, press, wire 6, press — and his Q1, Q2, Q4 deserve clean yes answers (order correct; presses are positions giving code 9-then-1, which matches the manual's "key that wears 9 / key that wears 1"; the manual is unconditional, so yes, all steps hold for any display — it went 8, 3, 6, 1, rising and falling, so it is no countdown and nothing keys off it).

The trap is Q3. Deaf never heard Blind speak (he can't), so he doesn't know Blind's actual capability list: "press slot 1–4, cut wire 1–6, no pinch, pull, twist or hold." He invented a menu of operations that don't exist on this bomb. Answering his menu would order an impossible or wrong action, so I reject it flat, then close the set by elimination: I tell him the only operations Blind's hands have are the pinch-sign and the press — so the pinch-thing must be Blind's one and only wire operation, whatever word Deaf uses for it. Deaf can relay that description to Blind by voice, and Blind — who owns the operation — will resolve it to "cut" himself. No new metaphor needs to survive translation.

Two corrections to relay, since Deaf can't hear Blind: Deaf misread Blind's gesture batch as "the fifth wire feels different" — false, and dangerous if Deaf treats wire 5 as special. Blind's true survey: six wires, all identical, ends alike. And the alignment bit is still outstanding — Blind counts wires from the keypad end, Deaf never said where his position 1 sits; until that's pinned, "wire 4" means different wires to their two numberings. I re-ask it as a clean yes/no: is wire one at the keypad end. I close with the hold sign: no GO this round — Deaf's GO trigger is a full all-yes confirmation, Q3's rejection breaks that, and I want Blind's spoken echo back through Deaf before I authorize anything.

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, please relay to Deaf word for word. Correction one: my open-palm sign meant HOLDING STEADY, not five - that is twice it has been read as five. Truth: I feel SIX wires and the FIFTH feels nothing different. I will never use that palm sign again. Correction two, the full tactile survey Deaf asked for: all six wires are identical under touch - none loose, none dead, none thin, thick, stiff or soft; no braille, notches or markings on the wire row. The only tactile markings on this whole bomb are the keypad digits - slot 1 raised 9, slot 2 raised 7, slot 3 raised 8, slot 4 raised 1, rigid keys, none pressed - and three strip glyphs, tactile-only: first and third identical like a V with a crossbar, middle one different like a rotated F. The keypad sits at the same end as my wire 1; I number wires from the keypad end. Now the narrowing that answers Deaf's question three: my bomb performs ONLY two operations - press slot 1 to 4, and cut wire 1 to 6. Pull out, tug once, hold three seconds are impossible here. So of Deaf's menu only two options can be true: skip the wires entirely, or pinch means CUT.
